title: Settings & Advanced
markdown:
**What it is:** The hub for power-user and admin tools that were pulled out of the day-to-day nav to keep it focused.

**What it does:**

- Links to Setup status, the Agent Council, Audit Log, Token Usage, this User Guide, the Architecture reference, Company Simulator, and Client Companies.
- Acts as a directory — each tile opens a dedicated screen.
- Keeps advanced configuration one click away without cluttering the main workspace.
- Shows whether the Executive is **running** or **paused**, with a switch to pause or resume it.
- Holds the **Workspace** card: whether you use Open Executive just for yourself or with your team, your role when it's just you, your time zone, and whether the Executive books meetings without asking.
- Holds the **Act as me** card, where the owner can let the Executive write email drafts as them, in their own voice, from their own Gmail.

**How to use:**

1. Click **Settings** at the bottom of the sidebar.
2. Click the tile for what you want to do:
   - **Setup status** — check that every part of your setup is working, and see what to do about anything that isn't.
   - **Agent Council** — change a specialist's model or prompt, or the Executive's voice.
   - **Audit log** — find out what the Executive did, and why.
   - **Token usage** — see what you're spending and where.
   - **User Guide** — this guide.
   - **Architecture** — the technical reference for how the system is built.
   - **Company Simulator** — try the Executive on a test company.
   - **Client Companies** — switch between clients if you do fractional work.

**Checking your setup:**

- Open **Settings → Setup status**. Each part of your setup gets a light: green is working, amber needs attention, red isn't working, grey isn't set up (and is optional).
- It tests things for real: the AI key, and each chat app's token, with a quick call that sends nothing. It also checks the Executive's email address, the company setup, the daily schedule, when and where your daily brief goes, and whether anyone on your team list can reach each chat app.
- Anything that isn't green says what to do in plain words, with a button when the fix is on another page. After you change a setting and restart the app, click **Check again**.

**Workspace:**

- **Using Open Executive** — **Just me** or **With your team**. You pick this when you first set up; change it here. Switching asks you to confirm and says what changes:
  - **Just me** pauses department check-ins and shows **Goals** (grouped by area) in the sidebar instead of Departments. Nothing is deleted — your departments stay, as the areas your goals are grouped by.
  - **With your team** brings back Departments and their daily check-ins, and the People and department cards on the Briefing.
- **Your role** (just you) — which describes you best (**Owner / founder**, **Executive inside an organisation**, **Independent or fractional**, or **Other**), your title, who you report to, what you're responsible for and what you're measured on. Every field is optional; click **Save role** after editing. The Executive uses it to fit its advice to your job — a VP gets help making the case to their boss, an owner gets help with a call that's theirs alone to make. It stays saved if you switch to your team.
- **Time zone** — when your morning brief, end-of-day digest and reflection arrive, and how the Executive reads "tomorrow at 9". It suggests the zone your browser is in; **Follow server default** uses the server's setting.
- **Book meetings without asking** — when on, the Executive books meetings on your calendar on its own; when off, each booking waits for your approval on the Briefing. (Shown only when your install supports it.)
- Only the principal can change the mode, role and time zone. A persona you customised in Council stays in place in either mode.

**Act as me:**

- Normally the Executive writes only as itself, from its own email account. **Act as me** lets it write an email *as you*: ask in chat — "reply to Dana as me: yes to the 5th" — and it saves a draft in **your own Gmail Drafts** for you to read, change and send. It never sends anything itself, and everything else it writes stays in its own name.
- For now only the owner (the principal) sees this card. It works when you ask in the web app, in a direct message to the Executive on Slack or Discord, or in a verified private Telegram chat — never in a shared channel or thread, from an email, a scheduled job or anyone else's conversation.
- **Your Gmail** — connect your own Gmail first. The card shows the command to run on a computer with a browser; sign in as yourself, put the file it writes where your install reads it, then click **Check again**. It won't connect the Executive's own address as yours.
- **Write drafts as me** — the switch. It stays off until your Gmail is connected, and turning it off applies from your next message.
- **How I write** — click **Learn from my sent mail** and it reads your recent sent emails once and describes how you write: your usual **Length** and **Tone**, a **Greeting** for your team, your contacts and anyone else ({first} stands for their first name), your **Sign-off**, your **Habits**, what you **Never** do, and a few **Examples of your writing** that set the tone. Change any of them and click **Save changes**; **Lock** stops it being relearned from your mail (you can still edit it); **Reset** starts over; **Remove examples** drops the examples. Your Gmail signature is added to every draft: **Refresh from Gmail** picks up a change you made to it in Gmail, **Don't add my signature** stops adding it, and **Add my Gmail signature** brings it back.
- In chat you get a card, "Drafted an email as you to …", that opens the draft in Gmail. If the Executive isn't sure about something, it asks you instead of guessing.

**Setting up just for yourself:**

- The first time you set up, Open Executive asks who it is for — **Just me** or **Me and my team** — before anything else, and saves your time zone from the browser. Re-running setup later skips this; change the mode here instead.
- **Just me** is for anyone who uses Open Executive just for themselves, whatever their role: your own business, a team you lead inside an organisation, or clients you advise as an independent or fractional executive.
- Choosing **Just me** then asks **What's your role?** — the same fields as **Your role** above. Fill in what you like, or click **Skip for now**.
- Just for yourself, the setup conversation asks about your work rather than your team, following the role you gave: an owner about what you offer, your customers, pricing, cash and runway; an executive inside an organisation about that organisation (it becomes your company profile), what you're responsible for, who you report to and what you're measured on; an independent about your practice and clients. Everyone is asked about their goals. On **Here's what I understood** there is a single **You** card (your name and role) next to **Your sign-in email**, instead of the team and department lists.
- The step-by-step form skips the team size, team members and fractional executives steps.
- In the sidebar, **You** holds **Goals**, **People** and your profile: **Business profile** if you own the business, **Your work** for any other role (or none). The profile page follows the same choice: for any other role it is worded around the organisation you work in (**Where You Work** in place of Company Basics). Either way departments are listed there as **Areas**, and your title, who you report to and what you're responsible for stay under **Your role** above.

**Pausing the Executive:**

- Click **Executive running** at the bottom of the sidebar (or use the card at the top of Settings), add a reason if you like, and click **Pause Executive**.
- While paused, the Executive starts nothing on its own: no briefs, nudges, monitoring, inbox processing or workflow timers. An amber banner appears on every page.
- Chat and direct messages (Slack, Telegram, Discord, Google Chat) still get answers.
- Nothing is lost. Work that falls due during the pause waits, and runs when you click **Resume**. The switch shows how many actions are waiting.
- Anyone who can sign in can pause the Executive, but only the principal can resume it.

*Tip: if you're looking for a feature that isn't in the sidebar, it's probably here. This guide is also pinned next to Settings at the bottom of the nav.*
